title: Security & Deployment Intake - Calypso Manufacturing
next_steps: Share SOC 2 Type II report and latest penetration test
Schedule SE-led private deployment tech deep dive (2 weeks)
Run a 48-hour dedicated capacity benchmark with sample workload
Provide draft retention & deletion policy template
action_items: Jordan Park | Send SOC2 + pen test links | 2026-12-12
Maya Singh | Prepare benchmark plan & tooling checklist | 2026-12-17
Evan Morales | Share sample traffic profile and PII/data classification | 2026-12-14
header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Evan Morales (Calypso Head of Infra), Priya Kapoor (Calypso CISO), Sam Lee (Platform Eng), Tara Huang (Compliance)
summary: High-level security intake focusing on SOC2/ISO readiness, SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit/logging and KMS integration. Calypso is leaning towards dedicated or private deployment due to regulated firmware IP and specific data residency requirements; they want to validate encryption at rest keys and audit trail retention. Agreed to run a short benchmark and follow up with detailed security docs.
topics: SSO (SAML) integration and SCIM RBAC mapping
Audit logs retention, tamper evidence and exportability
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
questions: How granular is RBAC and can it be mapped to our SCIM groups?
What audit log retention windows and formats are supported?
How are backups and snapshots encrypted and who holds keys?
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, account lead on Redwood. Maya and I will run through security intake. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Evan Morales: Doing well, thanks. Quick note we have Priya on who's leading security and Tara for compliance.
[00:14] Priya Kapoor: Hi all. We're trying to understand whether we can use Redwood hosted or if we need dedicated or private because we have IP in the models and strict data residency rules.
[00:25] Maya Singh: Totally, that's what we're here for. We'll go through SOC2/ISO, key management, SSO and RBAC mapping, and audit logs.
[00:33] Sam Lee: Great. To be clear we have some PII and also firmware design docs that we don't want leaving certain regions.
[00:40] Jordan Park: Understood. Quick question on timeline—are you looking to pilot in Q1?
[00:46] Evan Morales: Yeah ideally pilot end of Q1, production mid Q2 if things look good. Budget in place but need security sign off.
[00:52] Priya Kapoor: Our main redlines are: customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS), SOC2 Type II evidence, SSO with SAML and SCIM provisioning, RBAC controls tied to groups, and immutable audit logs kept for minimum 2 years.
[01:05] Maya Singh: Nice list. For SOC2 we have a Type II report and we can share the latest, it covers hosted environment. For Dedicated/Private customers we also provide architecture docs and deployment runbooks.
[01:16] Priya Kapoor: Is the SOC2 scoped to multi-tenant hosted? We need a clear scope statement.
[01:21] Jordan Park: Yes, our SOC2 covers the hosted API service; we'll send the scope page. For dedicated we have customer-specific attestations and can talk to third-party validators as needed.
[01:32] Tara Huang: About KMS—we need to know whether keys can be customer-owned and never seen by Redwood ops.
[01:38] Maya Singh: You can bring your own KMS in Dedicated and Private—HSM-backed keys are supported. For hosted there are BYOK patterns via customer-managed cloud KMS -- so Redwood never stores the plaintext keys. There's a small handshake for key rotation.
[01:52] Evan Morales: Can you be more specific: are keys used for everything at rest, model artifacts, snapshots, and backups?
[01:58] Maya Singh: Yes, encryption at rest covers model artifacts, tensors on disk, and backups. Snapshots are encrypted with your key in private/dedicated. For hosted we use envelope encryption with your KMS for the root key. Sometimes the transcript hear says envelop vs envelope which stumbles in auto text.
[02:15] Sam Lee: What's the fallback if the KMS region is different from compute region? We have data residency constraints.
[02:21] Jordan Park: We recommend colocating KMS and compute in the same cloud region for private/dedicated. For hosted we have region controls and can pin workloads to region, but some global control plane communications remain. We'll clarify in the deck.
[02:36] Priya Kapoor: RBAC—can we map SCIM groups to role levels? We need separation of duties between SRE, ML infra, and analysts.
[02:43] Maya Singh: Yes, SCIM provisioning can map to roles. We support role templates and custom roles for fine-grained policies. There's also token scoping for API calls.
[02:54] Evan Morales: How about audit logs? Format, tamper proofing, and export mechanisms?
[02:58] Maya Singh: We emit structured audit logs with timestamps, actor, request id, model version, and token counts. Logs are available via streaming to your SIEM (S3, CloudWatch, or syslog endpoint). For tamper evidence, logs are write-once in the managed stack and we support append-only retention and signing hashes for longer-term archival.
[03:20] Tara Huang: Do you provide log redaction? We need to avoid storing raw PII in logs for certain request types.
[03:27] Maya Singh: Yes, we can configure redaction rules and masking at the ingestion layer. Also recommend client-side filtering before sending if possible.
[03:35] Priya Kapoor: Retention windows—minimum 2 years, with export within 24 hours on request?
[03:41] Jordan Park: We can commit to configurable retention. Hosted default is 90 days, but for enterprise contracts we can extend retention and provide exports. We'll share a retention SLA example.
[03:52] Sam Lee: On the dedicated side, how isolated is network? Do you run in our VPC or do we have to connect via peering?
[03:59] Maya Singh: For Dedicated we can run either in a customer VPC or in a managed VPC with dedicated subnets. Private on-prem offers full air-gapped installs. We'll document those topologies; there's a tradeoff between ops burden and isolation.
[04:13] Evan Morales: Could you run a small on-prem pilot? Our legal team likes on-prem but it's a heavy lift.
[04:18] Jordan Park: We do offer an on-prem package for regulated customers but usually recommend Dedicated first. We'll put together the options and cost deltas.
[04:28] Priya Kapoor: What about compliance certifications besides SOC2—ISO 27001?
[04:33] Maya Singh: We're pursuing ISO; select customers have completed audits against ISO in private deployment contexts. We'll share current ISO status and timeline.
[04:42] Sam Lee: Any data residency constraints for model training? We're not training models with Redwood, only inference, but we store traces for evals.
[04:50] Maya Singh: Understood. Inference-only—traces and metrics can be routed to your region and we can disable retention for traces that contain sensitive content.
[05:00] Evan Morales: We also need detail on incident response and notification SLAs. If there's a compromise, what is your timeline?
[05:07] Jordan Park: We have an IR playbook—typical notification is within 72 hours for confirmed breaches; for critical incidents we do immediate notif to designated contacts. Enterprise customers can negotiate tighter timelines.
[05:18] Priya Kapoor: One concern: we've seen previous vendors obfuscate where audit logs are stored. We need explicit exportable logs in standard formats.
[05:26] Maya Singh: Totally. We provide logs in JSON/NDJSON and can push to your S3 or third-party SIEM. We'll include schema samples.
[05:36] Tara Huang: On SSO—SAML plus SCIM provisioning. How long to integrate with our identity provider and support MFA?
[05:44] Maya Singh: Usually 2-3 days to configure SAML/SCIM with Okta/Azure AD and test. MFA is enforced by your IdP. For RBAC we map groups to roles.
[05:53] Sam Lee: Does Redwood allow scoped API keys per model or per route? We want least privilege for inference agents.
[05:59] Jordan Park: Yes, token scoping is supported; you can scope keys to models, routes, and rate limits. Also token expiry and rotation are supported.
[06:09] Evan Morales: For benchmarks—we'd run a sample workload across models and seq-lengths, want to compare latency and cost. Can you do a 48-hour dedicated run?
[06:18] Maya Singh: Yep, we can provision dedicated capacity for a transient benchmark. We'll need sample payloads, QPS profile, and target latency bands.
[06:26] Priya Kapoor: Slight tangent: how do you handle third-party dependencies—are there embedded binaries or external services in the runtime?
[06:34] Maya Singh: We have a dependency inventory and can provide SBOMs for the runtime. For private deployments we can run audits together.
[06:44] Jordan Park: Quick check—anything else critical we haven't covered?
[06:47] Priya Kapoor: Encryption in transit—TLS mutual auth for internal service calls?
[06:52] Maya Singh: We support mTLS between internal services and can enable it for private/dedicated. For hosted the control plane uses TLS with strong ciphers.
[07:03] Evan Morales: About the legal process: do you have a standard DPA and data processing addendum we can review?
[07:09] Jordan Park: Yes we'll attach our DPA and standard enterprise terms. Legal can redline.
[07:15] Tara Huang: For auditability—are access reviews supported? We need quarterly access reviews and attestation logs.
[07:22] Maya Singh: We expose admin dashboards and audit exports to support reviews; we also have API endpoints to list active sessions and tokens for attestation.
[07:34] Sam Lee: A couple practical items—what's the observability surface? Can we get per-token cost telemetry?
[07:41] Jordan Park: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model. We'll demo that in the next call.
[07:50] Priya Kapoor: Regarding data deletion—can you perform targeted deletions by request id or user id? We need proof of deletion for compliance.
[07:57] Maya Singh: Yes, we support targeted deletions and audit entries for deletion operations. For hosted we keep immutable logs of deletions.
[08:07] Evan Morales: If we go dedicated, who owns the backups? Are we responsible for snapshot lifecycle?
[08:12] Maya Singh: Typically backups remain in the tenant's cloud account if we run in your VPC; if in managed VPC they live in a dedicated bucket with controlled access. Snapshot lifecycle policies can be defined per customer.
[08:25] Jordan Park: Let's recap next steps and owners. We'll send SOC2 & pen test, Maya will prepare benchmark plan, Evan will share traffic profile, and we'll schedule SE deep dive.
[08:36] Priya Kapoor: Sounds good. Please include the retention SLA and an example runbook for on-prem.
[08:42] Jordan Park: Noted. We'll aim to have docs in your inbox by Friday.
[08:46] Evan Morales: Thanks everyone.
[08:47] Maya Singh: Thanks. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench and tech deep dive.
[08:51] Jordan Park: End call.

Note: transcription contains occasional misheard words (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache) and speaker overlaps.
